claims.text: The as-cast EHEA has a dual-phase lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure.
The as-cast lamellar EHEA has limited room-temperature tensile ductility.
The as-cast lamellar EHEA has high strength.
Warm forging at 0.5–0.6Tm to a strain of 0.3–0.4, followed by a short low-temperature anneal, will refine the lamellar microstructure.
The proposed forging and annealing treatment will partially spheroidize the B2 and fcc phases.
The proposed treatment will reduce high-angle boundary facets.
High-angle colony-boundary facets act as crack-initiation sites in these EHEAs.
Moderately warm forging breaks up coarse lamellar boundaries.
Moderately warm forging introduces beneficial dislocation substructures.
A short post-forging anneal relieves internal stresses.
Lamellar refinement, spheroidization, boundary modification, and stress relief will reduce microcrack nucleation at colony interfaces.
The proposed microstructural changes will slow microcrack growth and improve accommodation of plastic strain.
The treatment will produce room-temperature tensile strength comparable to or somewhat greater than that of the as-cast baseline.
The treatment will increase room-temperature elongation to failure by multiple percentage points.
For the target EHEA, 800–900 °C corresponds to the proposed 0.5–0.6Tm forging range.
Forging above approximately 0.6Tm could cause excessive coarsening and offset ductility gains.
Extremely high forging strains could degrade the beneficial microstructure and offset ductility gains.
Inappropriate processing can produce grain growth, retained stress concentrations, or phase instability that negates the intended benefits.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis promises improvement in both strength and ductility beyond the baseline, whereas the predicted outcome allows strength merely to remain comparable to the baseline.
The hypothesis requires improved strength, but the falsification rule invalidates it only if strength is significantly lower, thereby allowing unchanged or modestly reduced strength.
